page: Microsoft Azure EC32es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the ECEV6 family, executed on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated 32-vCPU Intel Xeon TDX processor utilizing x86_64 architecture across 16 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at 4.2 GHz. The CPU features 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a massive 260 MB L3 cache, backed by instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography accelerators like AES and VAES.

The instance is provisioned with 256.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive enterprise footprints. It contains no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, relying entirely on remote premium storage capabilities for persistence and data operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the EC32es_v6 demonstrates top-quartile execution in Geekbench single-core (2032.0), multi-core (16308.0), image processing (15278.0), and text processing (2490.0), alongside strong PassMark physics computing (6400.56). General compute measures including PassMark CPU score (41674.85), stress-ng multi-core (28246.96), and Redis SET throughput (36.72 million operations per second) place in the average tier. Conversely, PassMark memory performance scored in the bottom 25% (1542.55).

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, this configuration delivers dense memory allocation alongside dedicated modern Intel Xeon compute without incurring costs for local NVMe disks or GPU silicon. Tradeoffs include reliance on networked storage for IO and weaker PassMark memory throughput metrics despite the high RAM capacity.

The EC32es_v6 is suited for large relational databases, in-memory caches, enterprise ERP systems, and memory-bound ETL workflows requiring broad instruction set acceleration without local storage dependencies.
